run:
account-values-20261117T092239Z; coverage/lab/server2025/account-values/account-values-result.json records all twenty observations passing. Four value-property families on the three account classes, each measured at create time and on an update, because that is where a provider's state and the directory come apart: the generic write sweeps establish that a write lands, and say nothing about what a value means after a round-trip.

account-expiration-values, success: a finite instant round-tripped as that exact instant at 100ns precision, and the same instant expressed in a non-UTC zone produced the same stamp rather than one shifted by the offset. Both documented never-expire sentinels, 0 and MaxInt64, read as never and carried no instant; clearing wrote MaxInt64 and left the attribute present, so a caller that cleared can see that it did; an update naming no expiry left the stamp untouched while a text write on the same call proved the update happened; and a create naming no expiry left the directory's own default. An attribute that was not read is reported as not read and never as never-expire, which is the distinction that would otherwise clear a caller's expiry out of state on any partial read. Failure: an instant mapping onto a sentinel, and an instant carrying sub-100ns precision, were both refused as invalid-request rather than adjusted or truncated.

binary-certificate-values, success: two values whose bytes include NUL and 0xFF round-tripped byte for byte through userCertificate, compared by SHA-256 digest. A cleared set and a field that was never requested read as distinguishable retrieval states, which is what stops a provider deleting certificates nobody mentioned. Clearing is reported unverifiable by design, because an absent attribute is equally what a denied read looks like, and the harness proves the effect with a read of its own. Failure: the same bytes offered to a text-typed property were refused as invalid-request, which is what makes the byte-exact claim a property of the binary path rather than of the directory accepting anything.

spn-multivalue-constraints, success: adding one value kept the others, including any the class owned before the harness touched it; a replace set exactly the requested values; a remove kept the rest; a clear emptied the attribute; and a value carrying non-ASCII text round-tripped. Only the service account offers a typed service principal name field, and it replaces the whole set rather than adding and removing values, so each observation records which door it used and what that door can express. Failure: a value another object already owns was refused with LDAP status 19 and the refused write left uSNChanged unchanged, and a value already present on the object was refused with LDAP status 20 on the explicit path and locally as a duplicate raw value on the typed path.

user-derived-property-roundtrips, success: HomeDirectory, HomeDrive, ProfilePath and Manager round-tripped through their typed fields, and Country and LogonWorkstations through explicit attribute changes, all carrying non-ASCII values; each reached the attribute recorded against it; an update naming none of them left every one unchanged; and no property disturbed another. Country and LogonWorkstations have no typed field on this surface, which the artifact records rather than hides. Failure: a manager that is not a distinguished name was refused as invalid-request with uSNChanged unchanged. This family also found and now guards an SDK defect: a creation composed its reported distinguished name from the schema's naming attribute, which spells it "cn", while the directory answers "CN". A caller that stored that name and wrote it back into a DN-valued attribute met a byte-exact readback comparison and was told the effect could not be verified, for a write that had landed correctly. Fixed by reporting the directory's own distinguishedName attribute, and measured here against the directory rather than against the SDK's own composition. The measurement also established why the first attempt at that fix changed nothing: a base-scoped search echoes the distinguished name the request supplied as the entry name, so only the attribute is authoritative. One limitation is recorded rather than fixed: a DN a caller spells with a non-canonical attribute type lands correctly but is reported uncertain rather than unverified. No variant state advances.
